problem_statement: The networking stack has no IPv4 routing capability. There is no way to install, look up, update, or delete IPv4 routes keyed by a destination prefix and a next-hop address, and no way to steer outgoing IPv4 packets toward the interface and next hop that a configured route selects. The expected behaviour is that IPv4 routes can be added (optionally with a next hop, or as an on-link route with no next hop), found by destination, deleted by entry or by next hop, expire by lifetime, respect route preference so a higher-preference route wins, resolve on-link destinations via the destination address itself rather than a next hop, and steer a routed IPv4 packet out the route's interface toward the resolved next hop (including handing off to ARP when the next hop is not yet link-layer resolved). A host route must also override the normally on-link interface for a destination.
twister_command: scripts/twister -p native_sim/native/64 -T tests/net/route/ipv4 -s tests/net/route/ipv4/net.route.ipv4 -s net.route.ipv4 -O twister-out --no-clean -W

verification.reason: The statement describes the IPv4 routing behaviour but omits all public API names (functions, Kconfig options, headers, struct fields, macros) that the tests rely on, and does not mention the renaming of the existing routing to IPv6-specific names. All gaps are in the public interface and can be repaired by adding the required names and signatures.

problems.detail: The statement gives no function names. The tests call net_route_ipv4_add, net_route_ipv4_del, net_route_ipv4_del_by_nexthop, net_route_ipv4_get_info, net_route_ipv4_get_nexthop, net_route_ipv4_lookup, net_route_ipv4_packet, net_route_ipv4_update_lifetime, and the renamed net_route_ipv6_* / net_route_ipv6_mcast_* functions. None are mentioned.

The statement gives no Kconfig option names. The tests and prj.conf use CONFIG_NET_IPV4_ROUTE, CONFIG_NET_IPV4_ROUTING, CONFIG_NET_IPV4_MAX_ROUTES, CONFIG_NET_IPV4_NBR_CACHE, CONFIG_NET_IPV4_ROUTE_LOG_LEVEL, and the renamed CONFIG_NET_IPV6_ROUTE, CONFIG_NET_IPV6_ROUTING, CONFIG_NET_IPV6_MAX_ROUTES, CONFIG_NET_IPV6_MAX_NEXTHOPS, CONFIG_NET_IPV6_ROUTE_MCAST, CONFIG_NET_IPV6_MAX_MCAST_ROUTES, CONFIG_NET_IPV6_MCAST_ROUTE_MAX_IFACES, CONFIG_NET_IPV6_MCAST_ROUTE_MLD_REPORTS, CONFIG_NET_IPV6_ROUTE_LOG_LEVEL. None are mentioned.
The statement gives no header file names. The tests include route_ipv4.h and route_ipv6.h. The statement only implies a header change.

The statement gives no struct field names. The tests access route->iface, route->addr.in_addr.s_addr, route->prefix_len, route->is_infinite, route->preference on struct net_route_entry, and net_route_ipv6_entry_mcast (renamed from net_route_entry_mcast). None are mentioned.
The statement gives no macro names. The tests use NET_ROUTE_INFINITE_LIFETIME, NET_ROUTE_PREFERENCE_LOW, NET_ROUTE_PREFERENCE_MEDIUM, NET_ROUTE_PREFERENCE_HIGH. None are mentioned.

The statement mentions on-link resolution and ARP handoff behaviour but does not name the new functions net_if_ipv4_addr_onlink(struct net_if **, const struct net_in_addr *) and net_pkt_ipv4_ll_resolve_addr(struct net_pkt *) that the tests call.

The statement only describes adding IPv4 routing but does not mention that the existing generic route API and Kconfig options must be renamed to be IPv6-specific. The hidden tests check the renamed IPv6 names throughout.

leak_check.leak_detail: Most of the new statement is allowed public interface: public function names/signatures, Kconfig options and their defaults, header paths, macro names/values, struct field names and the behaviours the tests check. The minor leak is the implementation-framing that goes beyond the public names: 'the existing generic route infrastructure must be made IPv6-specific' / 'must each be renamed with an ipv6 infix' / 'must be renamed to net_route_ipv6_entry_mcast' describe the refactoring approach rather than just the resulting public names; 'The header route.h must be split into route_ipv6.h ... and a new route_ipv4.h ... with route.h retaining only the shared definitions' describes internal header organization; and 'nexthop (a struct net_addr)' plus the addr in_addr internal layout describe internal struct layout the tests do not all access. None reveal an algorithm or the internal table/timer structures, so this is minor, not major.
leak_check.suggested_statement:
The networking stack has no IPv4 routing capability. There is no way to install, look up, update, or delete IPv4 routes keyed by a destination prefix and a next-hop address, and no way to steer outgoing IPv4 packets toward the interface and next hop that a configured route selects. The expected behaviour is that IPv4 routes can be added (optionally with a next hop, or as an on-link route with no next hop), found by destination, deleted by entry or by next hop, expire by lifetime, respect route preference so a higher-preference route wins, resolve on-link destinations via the destination address itself rather than a next hop, and steer a routed IPv4 packet out the route's interface toward the resolved next hop (including handing off to ARP when the next hop is not yet link-layer resolved). A host route must also override the normally on-link interface for a destination.

The existing IPv6 route infrastructure must be exposed under IPv6-specific public names so that IPv4-specific routing can coexist. The IPv6 route functions are named net_route_ipv6_add, net_route_ipv6_del, net_route_ipv6_del_by_nexthop, net_route_ipv6_lookup, net_route_ipv6_get_nexthop, net_route_ipv6_get_info, net_route_ipv6_update_lifetime, net_route_ipv6_foreach, net_route_ipv6_init, net_route_ipv6_packet, net_route_ipv6_mcast_add, net_route_ipv6_mcast_del, net_route_ipv6_mcast_lookup, net_route_ipv6_mcast_lookup_by_iface, net_route_ipv6_mcast_foreach, net_route_ipv6_mcast_forward_packet, net_route_ipv6_mcast_iface_add, and net_route_ipv6_mcast_iface_del. The multicast route entry type is named net_route_ipv6_entry_mcast. Public headers route_ipv6.h (IPv6 route API and multicast route type) and route_ipv4.h (IPv4 route API) are provided, and route.h keeps the shared definitions (struct net_route_entry, the preference and lifetime macros, and net_route_cb_t). The IPv6 Kconfig options are named CONFIG_NET_IPV6_ROUTE, CONFIG_NET_IPV6_ROUTING, CONFIG_NET_IPV6_MAX_ROUTES, CONFIG_NET_IPV6_MAX_NEXTHOPS, CONFIG_NET_IPV6_ROUTE_MCAST, CONFIG_NET_IPV6_MAX_MCAST_ROUTES, CONFIG_NET_IPV6_MCAST_ROUTE_MAX_IFACES, CONFIG_NET_IPV6_MCAST_ROUTE_MLD_REPORTS, and CONFIG_NET_IPV6_ROUTE_LOG_LEVEL.

The new IPv4 routing API must be declared in route_ipv4.h and must provide these functions:
- struct net_route_entry *net_route_ipv4_add(struct net_if *iface, struct net_in_addr *addr, uint8_t mask_len, struct net_in_addr *nexthop, uint32_t lifetime, uint8_t preference) — adds a route; nexthop may be NULL for an on-link route; returns the route entry or NULL.
- int net_route_ipv4_del(struct net_route_entry *entry) — deletes a route by entry; returns 0 on success, a negative error code otherwise.
- int net_route_ipv4_del_by_nexthop(struct net_if *iface, struct net_in_addr *nexthop) — deletes routes matching a next-hop on a given interface; returns the number of routes deleted (positive), or a negative error code (e.g. -ENOENT) if none match.
- void net_route_ipv4_update_lifetime(struct net_route_entry *route, uint32_t lifetime) — updates the lifetime of an existing route; a lifetime of NET_ROUTE_INFINITE_LIFETIME marks the route as infinite.
- struct net_in_addr *net_route_ipv4_get_nexthop(struct net_route_entry *entry) — returns a pointer to the next-hop IPv4 address of a route, or NULL for an on-link route.
- struct net_route_entry *net_route_ipv4_lookup(struct net_if *iface, struct net_in_addr *dst) — looks up the best-matching route by destination; returns the entry or NULL.
- bool net_route_ipv4_get_info(struct net_if *iface, struct net_in_addr *dst, struct net_route_entry **route, struct net_in_addr **nexthop) — resolves a destination to a route and next-hop; for an on-link destination the route is returned but the nexthop is the destination address itself; returns true if a route or on-link match is found.
- int net_route_ipv4_packet(struct net_pkt *pkt, struct net_in_addr *nexthop) — steers a packet toward the given next-hop, handing off to ARP when the next-hop is not yet link-layer resolved; returns 0 on success, negative on error.

New Kconfig options must be added: CONFIG_NET_IPV4_ROUTE (enables IPv4 route support; default y when CONFIG_NET_IPV4_NBR_CACHE is set), CONFIG_NET_IPV4_ROUTING (enables IPv4 IP routing between interfaces; depends on CONFIG_NET_IPV4_ROUTE), CONFIG_NET_IPV4_MAX_ROUTES (maximum number of IPv4 routing entries), CONFIG_NET_IPV4_NBR_CACHE (enables IPv4 neighbor cache), and a log-level option CONFIG_NET_IPV4_ROUTE_LOG_LEVEL for IPv4 route management.

The struct net_route_entry must expose the fields iface (struct net_if *), addr (holding an IPv4 address via its net_in_addr in_addr member), prefix_len (uint8_t), is_infinite (a boolean flag), and preference (uint8_t). When a route is stored the destination address must be normalised (masked to the prefix length). The macros NET_ROUTE_INFINITE_LIFETIME (value UINT32_MAX), NET_ROUTE_PREFERENCE_HIGH (value 0x01), NET_ROUTE_PREFERENCE_MEDIUM (value 0x00), and NET_ROUTE_PREFERENCE_LOW (value 0x03) must be defined in route.h and available to both IPv4 and IPv6 code.

A new function bool net_if_ipv4_addr_onlink(struct net_if **iface, const struct net_in_addr *addr) must be added; it determines whether the given IPv4 address falls within a subnet of the interface pointed to by *iface (or any interface if *iface is NULL), sets *iface to the matching interface, and returns true on success.

A new function const struct net_in_addr *net_pkt_ipv4_ll_resolve_addr(struct net_pkt *pkt) must be added; it returns the IPv4 address that a routed packet should have link-layer-resolved (set by net_route_ipv4_packet), or NULL if no resolve address is set.
